transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate you taking the time. 

Well, um... I guess I'm here because people keep telling me I'm not listening. I mean, I always try my best to be respectful and pay attention, I really do, but... my supervisor at the plant or my wife, they'll be talking straight to me, and then a minute later I kind of realize I only caught half of what they said. And then I have to ask them to say it again, which I always feel terrible about. 

I'm sure it's probably just normal distraction, you know? I don't want to make a big deal out of nothing. But they've been getting a little frustrated with me, so I just wanted to do the right thing and get it checked out. Is that... does that sound like an okay reason to be here?

When people are talking to you and you miss what they said, do you actually hear the sound of their voice but just don't process the words, or do you sometimes not hear them speaking in the first place?

Oh, right, yeah. Um... like I was just mentioning with my wife or my supervisor at the plant, when I end up having to ask them to repeat themselves... I definitely hear them talking. My hearing is fine, I promise! I would never just completely ignore them, I respect them way too much for that. 

It's more like... I hear the sound of their voice, but the actual words just sort of slip right past me? I'll be looking right at them, and I really am trying my hardest to be a good listener, but then a minute later I realize I only processed maybe half of what they meant. And that's when I have to apologize and ask them to say it again. I hate doing it because I know it makes it look like I don't care, but I really do. 

Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.

When you're doing something you really enjoy or find interesting—like a hobby or something at work that captures your attention—do you have the same trouble following along, or is it mainly when you're listening to things that feel more routine?

Oh, wow, um... that's a really good question. I've actually never thought about it like that. To be totally honest, I'm not really sure? 

I mean, I try my absolute best to give a hundred percent to everything, whether I'm tinkering with something in the garage or just sitting through the standard safety briefings at the plant. I'd hate to think I'm only tuning in when it's something fun for me, you know? That would be pretty selfish, and I really pride myself on being a hard worker and a good team player for the guys on the line. 

So... I guess I haven't really noticed if it's different depending on what I'm doing. I just try to be present for all of it. I'm sorry, I know that's probably not a very helpful answer. I can definitely try to pay more attention to that from now on if you want me to? Is it... is it okay that I don't really know?

When you're in a calm, relaxed situation with no stress or worries on your mind—like sitting on the couch at home in the evening—do you still have trouble following along when someone is talking to you, or does it seem to happen more when you're feeling stressed or anxious?

Oh, um... well, I try not to let myself get too stressed out, honestly. I always tell the guys at work that worrying just makes things harder, right? But... I guess if I'm just sitting on the couch with my wife, watching TV or something... I still end up asking her to repeat herself sometimes. 

I don't think it's because I'm anxious, though. I'm usually pretty relaxed at home. I just... I don't know, I guess my mind just wanders a little bit, even when everything is fine. I really hope she knows I'm not doing it on purpose, because I do love spending that quiet time with her. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I just want to be completely honest with you so you can help me figure this out. Is that the kind of information you were looking for?
How long have you been experiencing this trouble with listening and following along? Has this been happening your whole life, or did it start more recently?

Oh, um... well, I guess I've always been maybe a little bit scatterbrained? But I always managed just fine, really. It's only been, um... well, it's been this bad for about two years and two months, I'd say. 

That's right around when my wife started working outside the home. Which is wonderful, I'm so proud of her for it! But, um, it just meant that I had to step up and handle a lot more of the daily schedule on my own. I really try my absolute best to keep everything running smoothly so she doesn't have to worry, but... I guess having to juggle all those extra details is when the listening thing got a lot more noticeable for me. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound incapable, or like I'm complaining about helping out at home. I really do want to do my fair share, and I love supporting her! I just... I think that's when it really started getting harder to keep track of what people were saying. Is... is that the kind of timeline you were looking for?
Do you find yourself fidgeting a lot, or having trouble sitting still? Like, do your hands or legs tend to move around even when you're trying to stay focused?

Oh, um... yeah, I guess I do move around a bit. I really try to sit still, I promise I do, especially at work because I'd hate to be a distraction to the other guys. 

But... well, if I'm sitting in a safety huddle at the plant, or even just at the dinner table at home, my leg is almost always bouncing. Or my hands are messing with a pen, or jingling the keys in my pocket. Sometimes the guys at work will point it out and tell me I'm shaking the whole bench we're sitting on. I always feel terrible when they say that, I really don't mean to bother anyone or make them uncomfortable! 

I just... I guess my body just sort of likes to keep busy? I try to keep it under control so I don't look rude. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I don't care about what's going on. Is... is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find it hard to organize your day or plan out tasks ahead of time? Like, do you struggle to figure out what order to do things in, or do you often forget what you were supposed to do?

Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I like to think I'm pretty good at getting things done! I always make sure I show up for my shifts at the plant on time, and I try my hardest to keep on top of the chores at home so my wife doesn't have to stress about them. 

I guess sometimes I might, you know, start fixing something in the garage and then realize I need to mow the lawn first, but... I always get it all finished eventually! I don't really forget the big stuff. I try to write things down if I need to, so I don't let anyone down. I really want to make sure I'm doing my part. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering that right for you. I just wouldn't say I struggle with it, exactly... I just kind of take things as they come. Is that okay?
When you were a child in school, did your teachers ever comment on you having trouble paying attention in class, or did you find yourself fidgeting or having trouble sitting still back then?

Oh, um... gosh. Well, I suppose I've always been a little bit, you know, on the go. Even back when I was a kid. I really hope it doesn't make me sound like I was a bad student, because I always respected my teachers! I really did. 

But, um... yeah, especially before middle school, they did have to move my seat around a fair bit. I just had a really hard time staying put in my chair. And... well, I'd get so eager to participate that I'd kind of just call out the answers without waiting my turn. I also, um, I guess I had a bad habit of leaning over and butting into the other kids' work. I got into a little bit of trouble for that back then, but I promise I was just trying to be helpful and friendly! I really didn't mean to be disruptive to the class. 

Does... does that help? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
